owned_invariants: A request is closed: workflow, task, and optionally sealed and replies; any other field is refused as BAD_REQUEST. The task and the sealed part must be objects, and a reply is null or an object with the one key content.
The walk is a function of the request alone. The same request gives the same prompts, the same predicates and the same verdict.

The host writes every prompt. Before a prompt is returned or counted as asked it is passed through the sealed-value guard, and a prompt that carries a sealed value refuses the whole run as SEALED_LEAK, naming the stage.
A task the family cannot read is refused as BAD_TASK with the family's reason before any step is asked.

next returns the first step that has no reply, with its stage, its prompt and the prompt's SHA-256, or no step when the replies are enough for a verdict. judge refuses a run that still waits for a reply as REPLIES_INCOMPLETE, and both refuse replies beyond the end of the run.

Whatever a family's walk returns, a certified verdict or a typed refusal stands only when at least one predicate was recorded and every one passed. Otherwise the run is refused under the first failed predicate's name in capitals, or NO_HOST_PREDICATE when none was recorded, with the walk's claim kept in the detail.
A predicate name is recorded once. A second record under the same name is kept as a failed predicate named repeated:<name>, so the run cannot certify.

A report lists every predicate in the order it was recorded with the SHA-256 of the canonical text of its evidence, and every step that was asked with the SHA-256 of its prompt. judge answers PASS for HOST_CERTIFIED and TYPED_REFUSAL and FAIL for REFUSED.
A reply the walk cannot read gives the verdict REFUSED with the code MALFORMED_CANDIDATE and the reason; a null reply is the model giving none.
boundaries: The host does not call a model and does not see that a reply came from one, or from the prompt it wrote. The caller sends prompts and brings replies back.
The run budget and the transcript are kept by the caller.
A certified verdict covers the predicates listed with it on the replies in the request, and nothing else.
next_in and judge_in take the registry to use, so a family can be tested without being shipped. The command line always uses FAMILIES.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.

basis.G1: Module header declares AuthorityEffect None and the contract URN; public items match this contract and code/rust/pfp_operads/README.md. Not B: no requirement-to-symbol trace beyond the README and docs/plans/operads_redesign.md.
basis.G2: Non-numeric: counts of replies and steps, and SHA-256 digests asserted against digests the tests compute themselves. Not B: the hash library is trusted.
basis.G3: Typed refusal codes BAD_REQUEST, BAD_JSON, BAD_TASK, UNKNOWN_WORKFLOW, SEALED_LEAK, REPLIES_INCOMPLETE and ENCODING, each with a sentence. Replies are read with get, never by index. No unwrap or expect. Not B: panic-freedom is tested, not proven.
basis.G4: 31 protocol tests assert the listed registry, the exact default prompt and its hash, each refusal by code and message, the turn and the report field by field, repeated predicate names, a test family that claims a certified verdict or a typed refusal with no predicate or past a failed one, and the three commands of the binary with exit codes 0, 1 and 2. One mutant is recorded as demonstrably equivalent with its justification in the report. Mutation campaign R = 103/103. clippy -D warnings and rustfmt pass. Not B: mutants are hand-written one-line edits, not a generated campaign, and there are no generator-driven property tests.
basis.G5: Measured worst cyclomatic 15, cognitive complexity is not measured for Rust, nesting 3; ceiling B, recorded B.
